2. Pyramid of biomass The graphical representation of the biomass of organisms at different tropic levels

in an ecosystem is called pyramid of biomass. In grassland and forest ecosystem the biomass of producers is maximum and decreases gradually in successive trophic level. So, the pyramid is upright. In pond ecosystem, producers are found in large number but they are smaller in size so biomass is least. The biomass of consumers increases gradually in successive trophic level. The pyramid of biomass in pond ecosystem is inverted.

3. Pyramid of energy The graphical representation of the energy of organisms at different tropic levels

in an ecosystem is called pyramid of energy. The pyramid of energy is always upright, can never be inverted, because the flow of energy in a food chain is always unidirectional. Producers trap solar energy during photosynthesis process for the preparation of organic matter. These organic matters are transferred to next trophic level. When energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next trophic level, some energy is always lost as heat at each step. So, the pyramid is upright.

It is measured in KJ/m2year (Kilo Joule per square meter per year).

The productivity is of following types: 1. Primary productivity: The rate at which producers within ecosystem synthesize organic compounds from inorganic molecules using solar energy. It is of two types: a. Gross primary productivity (GPP): The total amount of organic of matter produced by producers though photosynthesis. b. Net primary productivity (NPP): The amount of organic matter that remains after subtracting the energy used by producers for respiration from the gross primary productivity. 2. Secondary productivity: The rate of storage of energy in consumers is secondary productivity. 4.1.9 BIOGEOCHEMICAL CYCLE You have already learnt that living organisms require several chemical elements for their life process. They may be used as part of their structural component or as parts of enzymes which influence various life processes. Nutrients are continuously exchanged between the organism and their physical environment.
The cyclic movement of inorganic nutrients or essential elements between abiotic environment and biotic communities is called biogeochemical cycle.

Biogeochemical cycle is of three types: hydrological cycle (water cycle), gaseous cycles (e.g. Carbon cycle, oxygen cycle, nitrogen cycle etc.) and sedimentary cycle (like, phosphorous cycle, calcium cycle, sulphur cycle, etc.).
